| `20260814.083000` | [`20260814-083000_fora14-constel-snapshot-log-compaction.bron`](20260814-083000_fora14-constel-snapshot-log-compaction.bron) | **FORA14 — Constel snapshot: compact the log so it can serve forever** — FORA12 built the append-only replicated log every consensus exists to produce and FORA13 let the sky change its own stars, yet both leave one honest bound: the log is a fixed `[max_entries]u32` refusing `LogFull` at the cap. The state a log accumulates is a **deterministic, order-sensitive fold** (`state_n = state_{n-1} *% fold_mul +% value_n`, wrapping) — order-sensitive on purpose, so the same values in a different order fold to a different state and a `Snapshot` preserves the log's *ordering*, not merely its multiset. A **link** is a `kind_tax` fact whose signed body is `L·id(16)·seq·last·to(32)` — a transfer from the signer to `to`, sequence `seq` of the braid named by `id`, `last=1` closing the chain; every link may carry a **different** signer (the chain routes coins hand to hand). Links chain causally on the Cord (l0→l1→l2), so the agreed order always places them in sequence. When the final link closes the chain, `settle_braid` evaluates it as **one atom** — a forward affordability walk over a bounded scratch table seeded from real balances: if **every** link affords, the whole braid commits (every coin moves); if **any** cannot, the whole braid rejects (not one coin moves, not even the earlier links that afford alone). **The crux:** a 3-link braid Alice→Bob→Carol→Dave whose final step (Carol holds 120, asked 200) overdraws reverses WHOLE — Alice 100, Bob 50, Carol 0, Dave 0, no trace left; the committing twin (final 60) moves every coin (Alice 0, Bob 30, Carol 60, Dave 60); a chain whose final link never arrives stays **pending**. The heir's acceptance is signed over a tag, the estate id, and the two points, so it cannot be lifted from one estate to another. A `Keyring` maps a point to its keeper key (the caller's statement of whose word to trust, as `council_sky_signed` maps a seat to its key); `verify_directive`/`verify_acceptance` touch no estate, so a traveled record (r3) can re-check offline. Refusals hold — a tampered will (`BadConsent`, never sealed), a forged directive or forged acceptance by a stranger (`BadConsent`), an unenrolled party (`UnknownKeeper`, before the estate is touched), a cross-estate signature (`BadConsent`). Succession itself is rung one's unchanged two-proof gate, so a signed round still needs both a sealed directive and an acceptance. Additive — rung one grew only two pub readers (`item_at`, `disposition_at`) so r2 can digest the marks; r1 re-runs GREEN.
